title: Core-banking candidate knowledge: patterns, tactics and anti-patterns

authority: Candidate only. Nothing in this file is approved, released or active. No runtime module reads it: it informs no score, no hard constraint, no conformance result, no draft, no Brain retrieval and no lens reading. It becomes knowledge only when a four-eyes knowledge approver attaches the exact source passages, checks each statement against them, and releases the resulting claims through the governed path (knowledge.source, knowledge.claim, knowledge.review by another person, knowledge.release, knowledge.activate).
sourcePolicy: A source is named only where its title, edition and section can be given precisely; otherwise source is null and sourceNeeded is true. No passage was retrieved, attached or hashed for any entry, and no rights were checked. 'located' says how the title and section were found: 'confirmed against public summaries on 2026-10-07' (the section's number and title were checked against public summaries of the text, not against the text itself), or 'from the drafter's reading, not confirmed'. 'supports' says what the entry relies on the passage for; the approver checks that the passage says it.

entries.title: Balanced, referenced posting
entries.intent: Record every financial event as one posting of two or more entries whose debits equal its credits in each currency, under one unique reference, and refuse a posting that does not balance.

source.author: Luca Pacioli
source.section: Distinctio IX, Tractatus XI, Particularis de computis et scripturis
source.supports: The double-entry method: each transaction entered in the journal is posted twice in the ledger, once as a debit and once as a credit.

source.author: Martin Fowler

entries.title: Correct by reversal, never by edit
entries.intent: Never change or delete a posted entry; correct an error with a reversing posting and, where needed, a new correct posting, both linked to the original.

entries.title: Suspense with an owner and an age limit
entries.intent: Send entries that cannot be applied to their account to a suspense account with an owner, a reason and a deadline, and clear them by posting, not by editing.

entries.title: Single-sided balance update
entries.intent: Changing an account balance directly, without a balancing entry and a reference, so that the ledger can no longer show where the money came from.

entries.title: Money as a floating-point number
entries.intent: Holding amounts as binary floating-point numbers, so that sums drift by fractions of the minor unit and postings stop balancing.

entries.title: Dated, ordered and restartable end-of-day chain
entries.intent: Run end of day as an ordered chain of steps under one business date, each step idempotent and checkpointed, so that a failed run restarts from the last completed step without posting twice.

entries.title: Cut-off, then date roll
entries.intent: Stop accepting postings for the closing business date at a stated cut-off, give later postings the next business date, and roll the date only after the closing steps finish.

entries.title: Stay online while end of day runs
entries.intent: Keep the channels open during end of day by accepting transactions against the next business date and applying them in order once the run completes.

entries.title: End of day that can only start over
entries.intent: An end-of-day run that cannot restart from a failed step, so a failure late in the window forces a full rerun or a manual repair of postings.

entries.title: Daily accrual on a stated day-count basis
entries.intent: Accrue interest every day on each account's stated day-count basis and rate, record each accrual as a posting, and capitalise or pay it on the product's schedule.

entries.title: Charges from dated tariff tables
entries.intent: Compute charges and fees from tariff tables keyed by product and event, each version with an effective date, so that a past charge can be recomputed with the tariff that applied then.

entries.title: Rates and fees written into programs
entries.intent: Interest rates, fees and tax rates written into program code, so that every change needs a release and the values that applied in the past are lost.

entries.title: Every amount with its currency
entries.intent: Keep every amount with its ISO 4217 currency code and that currency's minor unit, and never add amounts of different currencies without a conversion at a recorded rate.
